lines.trans: Chef, it seems the end has come for me now.
Keep quiet and listen to the jury's strict verdict.
Victoria chose this first dish in particular.
And the second fish she called awful?
She didn't recommend it to anyone in the hall.
Congratulations, our cook won fairly today!
Thank you very much for the great, fair evaluation.
Lord, how incredibly delicious this is!
Chef, let me taste a little too.
Wait, I haven't properly tasted it myself yet.
And the losing cook must finish eating everything himself.
I hope our guests will remain very pleased.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('so, and what about') (starting a question: а жвачку?) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'dish', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: This is the restaurant's signature dish.

examples.text: Настоящий повар чувствует каждый вкус блюда.
examples.trans: A real chef feels every taste of the dish.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('big, large').

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('into, to') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'verdict', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: The judge delivered a strict verdict.

examples.text: Молчи и слушай строгий вердикт жюри.
examples.trans: Keep quiet and listen to the jury's strict verdict.

meanings.note: predicative: очень вкусно = it's delicious
Secondary conversational sense ('deliciously') (вкусно готовить = to cook well) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
ends a conversation or an order: 'Всё, свободен' = that's all, you can go
Secondary conversational sense ('that's it, done') (at the start of a sentence) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'second', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.en: to choose, select; to use up completely (quotas, limits)
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'брать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to choose', forming an aspectual pair with 'выбирать'.

examples.text: В этом году все квоты выбрали.
examples.trans: This year all the quotas have been used up.
She chose the most beautiful dress.
Agreed, I will choose a movie.

meanings.note: Expressive conversational Russian interjection or greeting ('Good Lord!') used directly in spoken exchanges.
Abstract masculine noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-ость', denoting the quality or state of 'guest'.

examples.trans: All the guests love them very much.

examples.text: Сегодня вечером к нам придут гости.
examples.trans: Guests are coming to our place tonight.

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to give', forming an aspectual pair with 'давать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: short form: ты довольна? = are you happy?

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'есть'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to finish eating', forming an aspectual pair with 'доедать'.

examples.text: Он доел весь суп до конца.
examples.trans: He finished eating all the soup to the end.

examples.text: А проигравший повар обязан доесть всё сам.
examples.trans: And the losing cook must finish eating everything himself.

meanings.note: in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see
Secondary conversational sense ('still, yet') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('even (with comparatives)') (ещё больше = even more) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'jury', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: Members of the jury are tasting dishes.

examples.text: Молчи и слушай строгий вердикт жюри.
examples.trans: Keep quiet and listen to the jury's strict verdict.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'for' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('behind') (+ instrumental) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Declinable masculine noun meaning 'hall', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('living room') (regional/colloquial) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Understood. And who is managing the dining room?

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: вот именно = that's just it, quite right
Secondary conversational sense ('namely') (а именно = namely) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Именно это я и хотел сказать.
examples.trans: That is justamente what I wanted to say.

examples.text: Вот именно. Но мне сдаваться нельзя.
examples.trans: Exactly. But I must not give up.

meanings.note: мне кажется = I think, it seems to me
Secondary conversational sense ('it seems, I think') (кажется as a parenthetical word) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I think I've seen you somewhere.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'how'.
Secondary conversational sense ('as') (как вы знаете = as you know) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: the 'е' drops out in the other forms
Secondary conversational sense ('' ' = over and out') (radio and phone phrase) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: At the end of the film everyone is happy.

молчать.gloss: to be silent, to say nothing

meanings.en: to be silent, to keep quiet
meanings.note: почему ты молчишь? = why aren't you saying anything?

examples.text: Ну что ты молчишь? Ты толстый, ты не спортсмен!
examples.trans: Well, why are you so quiet? You're fat, you're no athlete!

examples.text: Молчи лучше, пока шеф не заметил нашу ошибку!
examples.trans: Better keep quiet before the chef notices our mistake!

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'деяться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hope, to rely on', paired with 'понадеяться'.

examples.trans: I hope so. Go on, act quickly!

meanings.note: кого + instrumental: назвать меня плохим словом
Secondary conversational sense ('to name') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: You called me a bad word.
What will you name your son?

examples.text: Ты назвал меня плохим словом. Меня, начальника!
examples.trans: You called me a bad word. Me, your boss!

наступить.gloss: to come (of time); to step on

meanings.en: to come, to set in (night, winter, a moment)
meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'ступить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to come', forming an aspectual pair with 'наступать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to step on') (наступить на + accusative) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, Аркаша? Наступила ночь, просыпается мафия.
examples.trans: So, Arkasha? Night has fallen, the mafia wakes up.

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'incredibly'.

examples.trans: Today you were simply incredibly lucky.

examples.text: Молчи, сегодня тебе просто невероятно повезло.
examples.trans: Keep quiet, today you were simply incredibly lucky.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'много'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to do a bit of work.

examples.text: Мы даём вам ещё немного времени.
examples.trans: We are giving you a little more time.

meanings.note: needs 'не' with the verb: никто не войдёт

examples.trans: I know the town like nobody else.

examples.text: Садитесь и держите дверь. Никто не войдёт.
examples.trans: Sit down and hold the door. Nobody will come in.

meanings.note: usually in short form обязан/обязана + dative + instrumental

examples.trans: You are obliged to come on time.

examples.text: Ты выпустишь меня под подписку о невыезде. И ты мне больше ничем не обязан.
examples.trans: You'll release me on a travel ban. And you won't owe me anything anymore.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('she') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: ничего не осталось = there's nothing left
Secondary conversational sense ('to stay') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'личный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('excellent').

examples.text: Квартира будет отличная. На Симашко есть новый дом.
examples.trans: It'll be an excellent flat. There's a new building on Simashko Street.

meanings.note: Derived feminine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'evaluation'.

examples.trans: The critic gave a high rating to the restaurant.

examples.text: Погоди, нам нужна более объективная оценка.
examples.trans: Wait, we need a more objective opinion.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'very'.
Secondary conversational sense ('very much') (with verbs: очень люблю) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'first', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Ты не понимаешь с первого раза?
examples.trans: You don't understand the first time?

examples.text: Ты что, с первого раза не понимаешь?
examples.trans: What, you don't understand the first time?

meanings.en: to defeat, to beat, to win
meanings.note: 1st person singular is not used in standard Russian
Declinable masculine noun meaning 'cook', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Есть такой английский повар. Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: There is this English chef. I will learn to cook from his shows.

examples.text: Я хочу работать поваром в ресторане.
examples.trans: I want to work as a cook in a restaurant.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to wait', forming an aspectual pair with 'ждать'.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'здравлять'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to congratulate', forming an aspectual pair with 'поздравить'.

meanings.en: to try, to taste (food or drink)
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'пробовать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to try', forming an aspectual pair with 'пробовать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to try, to attempt') (+ infinitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Try the tea with bread rings.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'советовать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to advise, suggest'.

examples.text: Она не посоветовала её никому в зале.
examples.trans: She didn't recommend it to anyone in the hall.

meanings.note: money, a game, a bet, or an election

examples.trans: I lost it on the stock exchange.

examples.text: Денег нет, Самсон. Я их на бирже проиграл.
examples.trans: There is no money, Samson. I lost it on the stock exchange.

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'пробовать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to taste properly', forming an aspectual pair with 'пробовать'.

examples.text: Шеф ещё не распробовал новое блюдо.
examples.trans: The chef hasn't properly tasted the new dish yet.

examples.text: Подожди, я сам ещё не распробовал.
examples.trans: Wait, I haven't properly tasted it myself yet.

examples.text: Но вы обязаны распробовать этот редкий шедевр!
examples.trans: But you must taste this rare masterpiece!

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'fish', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: A big platter of fish and crabs.

examples.text: На ужин мы приготовили свежую рыбу.
examples.trans: For dinner we cooked fresh fish.

examples.text: У нас есть большая тарелка рыбы и крабов.
examples.trans: We have a big platter of fish and crabs.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('oneself') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'today'.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Secondary conversational sense ('in a moment') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to listen', forming an aspectual pair with 'послушать'.
the imperative 'слушай' starts a sentence, like 'look, ...'
Secondary conversational sense ('hello (on the phone)') ('Слушаю' = I'm listening) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.

meanings.note: спасибо за + accusative = thank you for

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'fair', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Это было справедливое наказание для хулиганов.
examples.trans: That was a fair punishment for the troublemakers.

examples.text: Дмитрий, спасибо вам за справедливое решение.
examples.trans: Dmitry, thank you for the fair decision.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'трогий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('strict, stern').

examples.trans: How strict you are, Klavdia Viktorovna.

examples.text: У нас в школе очень строгий директор.
examples.trans: We have a very strict principal at our school.

examples.text: Ой, спина не разгибается! Какая вы строгая, Клавдия Викторовна.
examples.trans: Ow, my back won't straighten! How strict you are, Klavdia Viktorovna.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'too'.

examples.text: Мы же здесь выросли. И о людях тоже надо думать.
examples.trans: After all, we grew up here. And you have to think about people too.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'жасный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('horrible, terrible').

examples.trans: What a horrible person you are!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Do you want me to tell you honestly?

examples.text: Всё честно, Лёха. Взрослые не умеют ждать.
examples.trans: It's all fair, Lyokha. Grown-ups can't wait.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
